Aunt
ANT
n. (the wife of a father's brother; a relation named in the law of forbidden degrees)
From Latin amita, a father's sister, through Old French ante. The Authorized Version uses it once, in Leviticus 18, naming the wife of a father's brother as one of the near kin a man may not approach.

Biblical Definition

Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father's brother, thou shalt not approach to his wife: she is thine aunt. The verse belongs to the chapter that defines the forbidden degrees of marriage, and the chapter opens with a principle rather than a list: none of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to him, to uncover their nakedness: I am the LORD. Then the relations are enumerated one by one, mother, father's wife, sister, granddaughter, aunt, daughter in law, brother's wife, and the rest, so that no household could plead ignorance. The chapter grounds all of it in the character of God and the history of the nations: defile not ye yourselves in any of these things, for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you. The land itself is said to vomit out its inhabitants for these practices. And the chapter closes by naming them abominable customs, with the command, therefore shall ye keep mine ordinance, that ye commit not any one of these abominable customs, which were committed before you. The sexual law is covenant law, national in its consequences, and rooted in who God is.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): the sister of one's father or mother, and correlatively the wife of one's uncle; in Scripture, a relation within the forbidden degrees.

expand to see more

AUNT, n. The sister of one's father or mother; correlative to nephew or niece.

KINDRED, n. Relation by birth; consanguinity; relatives by blood.

AFFINITY, n. The relation contracted by marriage, between a husband and his wife's kindred.

INCEST, n. The crime of cohabitation or sexual commerce between persons related within the degrees wherein marriage is prohibited.

ORDINANCE, n. A rule established by authority; a permanent rule of action.

Key Scripture

Lev 18:14 — "Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father's brother, thou shalt not approach to his wife: she is thine aunt."

Lev 18:6 — "None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to him, to uncover their nakedness: I am the LORD."

Lev 18:24 — "Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you:"

Lev 18:30 — "Therefore shall ye keep mine ordinance, that ye commit not any one of these abominable customs, which were committed before you, and that ye defile not yourselves therein: I am the LORD your God."

Modern Corruption

Sexual boundaries are treated as private arrangements between consenting adults with no bearing on anyone else; Leviticus 18 grounds them in God's character, assigns them to households, and attaches national consequences.

expand to see more

The consent framework is the governing sexual ethic of the age, and Leviticus 18 was written against its ancestor. The chapter does not ask whether the parties agreed. It names relations, fixes limits by kinship and covenant, and repeats I am the LORD like a refrain through the whole catalogue, because the authority for the limit is the Lawgiver and not the participants. The same chapter goes on to name the sacrifice of children to Molech and homosexual practice and bestiality in the same list and under the same sanction, and calls the whole set abominations for which the land spued out its inhabitants.

The corruption in the church takes the softer form of treating these chapters as ceremonial and therefore obsolete. The New Testament does not read them that way. Paul dealt with a case at Corinth of a man having his father's wife — a Leviticus 18 offence — and treated it as fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, requiring discipline. The moral law binds still, the household is still the unit God addresses, and the dictionary holds marriage to be one man and one woman covenanting before God for life, within the degrees Scripture permits.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew dodah (H1733), an aunt, the wife of a father's brother; she'er (H7607), flesh, and so near kin; to'ebah (H8441), abomination.

Hebrew dodah (H1733) — an aunt, the wife of an uncle; she is thine aunt.

Hebrew dowd (H1730) — an uncle, a beloved one; thy father's brother.

Hebrew she'er (H7607) — flesh, and so blood relation; any that is near of kin.

Hebrew to'ebah (H8441) — an abomination, a detested thing; these abominable customs.

Usage

"“thou shalt not approach to his wife: she is thine aunt” — the single occurrence."

"“None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin” — the principle of the chapter."

"“I am the LORD” — the refrain that supplies the authority."
